cover_letter.name: Anthropic cover letter
body_paragraphs: The App Foundations team is deciding how memory, voice mode and artifacts feel to tens of millions of people, most of whom never think about the model underneath. That is the kind of problem I like: an everyday experience where small details decide whether something becomes a habit. Since 2022 I have owned that question for a 12M-user consumer app at Brightpath, across web, iOS and Android.

At Brightpath I rebuilt onboarding around a personalised first session and took day-7 retention from 31% to 39%. I run more than 60 experiments a year with a squad of design, engineering and data science, and I pair the numbers with weekly user interviews before making a call. I read the data myself in SQL and Amplitude, so the prioritisation rests on results I have checked.

I have not yet shipped a product built on a frontier model, and I would be learning how model capabilities turn into product from people who know them best. What I would bring is care for craft, a habit of testing before committing, and experience scaling consumer products without losing quality. I would welcome a conversation about where App Foundations is focused next.

autofill.why do you want to work at anthropic?: I want to work on consumer AI that people can trust, at a company that treats safety as part of the product. Claude's everyday experience, from memory to voice, is the kind of habit-forming, detail-heavy product work I do at Brightpath on a 12M-user app, and I would like to bring that craft to a product with this much reach.
autofill.describe a product experience you improv: Brightpath's first session. People opened the app, saw a generic library and left. We rebuilt it around one personalised session chosen from three onboarding answers, and tuned copy, timing and the moment we asked for notifications. Day-7 retention rose from 31% to 39% and trial starts by 22%.
autofill.describe a time you used data to make a: At Tidewell, drop-off between sign-up and the first linked account was our biggest leak. I broke the funnel down by step, found the bank-linking screen lost the most people, and we redesigned it with in-app education. Drop-off fell by 28%. I like decisions where the metric points at one clear step.
autofill._default: I enjoy owning a consumer experience end to end: research, experiments and shipping with design and engineering. This role is a close match for my work at Brightpath, and I would be glad to talk through the details and what the team is solving next.

body_paragraphs: Bits sits at a hard point in product design: it has to pay streamers well and still feel fun to viewers on a phone. I have spent my career on that balance for consumer subscriptions, where revenue only counts if people stay. That is why the Commerce role on Twitch's interactive products stands out to me.

At Brightpath I launched a family plan and ran annual-plan paywall tests that added $9M in recurring revenue, inside a program of 60+ experiments a year. At Tidewell, automated round-up savings grew monthly active savers by 47%, a feature built around a small, repeated action. I work in SQL and Amplitude and set the metrics myself with a 6-person squad.

I have not worked on live streaming or a virtual currency, and I would start by watching how streamers and viewers use Bits today. I would bring a monetization record, mobile-first habits and a steady experiment cadence. I would be glad to talk through the roadmap you have in mind, the metrics streamers care about most, and where you see the biggest openings for mobile commerce.

autofill.why do you want to work at twitch?: I want to work on monetization where the community is part of the product. Bits has to reward streamers and stay enjoyable for viewers on mobile, and that two-sided balance is the part of subscriptions I find most interesting. At Brightpath I added $9M in recurring revenue through paywall tests, and I would like to apply that rigor to creator earnings.
autofill.describe your experience with monetizati: At Brightpath I launched a family plan and ran annual-plan paywall tests that added $9M in annual recurring revenue. I design the test, agree the success metric with data science and read the result by cohort. Earlier, I owned round-up savings at Tidewell, which grew monthly active savers by 47% in two quarters.
autofill.how do you balance creator earnings with: I have not worked with creators directly, but the same tension shows up in subscriptions: a paywall that lifts revenue can hurt retention. My approach is to measure both sides of every test, revenue and retention, and ship only when the second does not suffer. I would apply that two-sided measurement to Bits.
autofill._default: I enjoy owning a consumer metric end to end, from research to experiments to launch. This role combines mobile products, monetization and a lively community, which is a close match for my subscription work at Brightpath, and I would be glad to talk through the details.

cover_letter.name: WHOOP cover letter
body_paragraphs: WHOOP's growth team is asked to own how members are acquired, converted and kept, with measurable goals attached. I do that today at Brightpath, a wellness subscription app with 12M monthly users, where I own the growth roadmap and the experimentation program behind it. The Senior Product Manager, Growth role feels like a natural next step.

At Brightpath I rebuilt onboarding and raised day-7 retention from 31% to 39%, then added $9M in recurring revenue through a family plan and annual-plan paywall tests. I run 60+ A/B tests a year with a 38% win rate, and I query my own data in SQL and Amplitude. At Tidewell, lifecycle messaging reactivated 180K dormant users.

I have led a 6-person squad but have not formally mentored other product managers, and I would like to grow that side of the craft at WHOOP. I would bring clear written strategy, honest experiment readouts and real interest in the product. I would be glad to talk through your growth priorities and how the team is organised today.

autofill.why do you want to work at whoop?: I want to work on a subscription product built around health, where retention depends on members seeing real value. At Brightpath I own growth for a wellness app, and WHOOP's focus on conversion, activation and long-term membership is the same funnel with higher stakes. I would like to bring a disciplined experimentation habit to your growth team.
autofill.describe your experience running an expe: At Brightpath I run 60+ A/B tests a year with a 38% win rate. Each test starts with an explicit hypothesis and a success metric agreed with data science, and I write up every result, wins and losses, so the roadmap compounds. Those tests rebuilt onboarding, lifting day-7 retention from 31% to 39%, and tuned the paywall.
autofill.have you mentored other product managers: Not formally. I run a 6-person growth squad at Brightpath and regularly share experiment readouts and PRD templates with colleagues, but I have not had product managers report to me. I would welcome the chance to grow that skill at WHOOP and to raise the craft bar through reviews and examples.
autofill._default: I enjoy owning the growth funnel for a subscription product, from onboarding to retention, using experiments to decide what to build. WHOOP's mission and its focus on member value are a close match for my work at Brightpath, and I would be glad to discuss the role.
